options.how: Arthur's movement runs through a realistic animation system, so starting, stopping and turning take visible time and every step feels heavy.
Faith keeps speed by chaining wall-runs, leaps and vaults across rooftops; breaking the flow costs momentum.

sources.note: Red Dead Redemption 2: heavy, animation-led controls described as a deliberate choice for a weighty, realistic world
Mirror's Edge: string together wall-runs, leaps and vaults in fluid movement; the flow keeps you running

options.how: Rotoscoped animation makes each move deliberate: jumps need a run-up, the prince hangs from ledges by his fingers, and long falls hurt or kill.
Speed builds on slopes and carries through loops, springs and rolls, so momentum rather than precise steps drives play.

sources.note: Prince of Persia: rotoscoped, lifelike movement; every jump has tension and the prince has weight; falls really hurt
Sonic the Hedgehog: engine built for speed and world physics; loops and slopes need built-up momentum

options.how: Levels sit on a block grid and Lara's standing and running jumps cover fixed distances, so players line up and plan each leap.
Triple jumps, long jumps, backflips and wall kicks chain into fluid routes, with air control to correct mistakes.

sources.note: Tomb Raider (1996): grid-based movement and jumps
Super Mario 64: triple jump, long jump and wall kick

options.how: Cargo weight and its placement shift Sam's balance; heavy loads make him lean and stumble on slopes, and the triggers steady him.
Double jump, two-charge dashes and monkey bars keep the Slayer airborne and circling arenas, dodging by movement instead of cover.

sources.note: Death Stranding: guide to walking, balance, cargo weight and terrain
Doom Eternal: dash, double jump, monkey bars and climbable walls used in arenas and traversal

options.how: The boy walks and jumps with modest range while ropes, boxes and traps follow physics, so careful, grounded movement avoids death.
Meat Boy accelerates fast, wall-jumps and steers sharply mid-air, so levels are run at speed as one flowing sequence.

sources.note: Limbo: physics puzzle platformer
Super Meat Boy: twitch reflex platforming

options.how: Attacks lock the hunter into long, committed animations with no canceling into movement, so positioning before each swing decides the fight.
Bullet jumps, double jumps, wall dashes and aim glides chain together; a double jump keeps existing momentum and wall contact resets air moves.

sources.note: Monster Hunter: World: committed attack animations give up the ability to move and force players to stick with decisions
Warframe: bullet jump, double jump keeps momentum, wall dash and latch reset air moves, aim glide

options.how: Jump, air-dash and climb with tight air control; each screen demands exact inputs and respawns are near instant.
No precision jumps: the challenge is carrying cargo over rough terrain, keeping balance under weight and planning the route.

sources.note: Celeste: jump, air-dash and climb, lightning-fast respawns
Death Stranding Director's Cut: store page

note: seed item: accuracy checked by the project owner

options.how: Kirby can inflate and hover indefinitely, so most gaps and pits are flown over rather than jumped with timing.
Momentum-based runs and wall jumps through mine-filled rooms, where one touch of a hazard kills the ninja.

sources.note: Kirby's Dream Land: Kirby can hover indefinitely
N++: fast-paced, momentum-based platformer

options.how: The flutter jump keeps Yoshi airborne for a moment, so short jumps can be stretched and corrected across gaps.
Twitch-reflex platforming through saws and spikes; Meat Boy dies often and levels demand exact jumps and wall jumps.

sources.note: Super Mario World 2: Yoshi's Island: flutter jump keeps Yoshi airborne to cross gaps
Super Meat Boy: tough-as-nails, twitch reflex platformer

options.game: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
options.how: There is no jump button: Link leaps automatically when running off a ledge, so platforming is about direction, not timing.
A rhythm-based runner where a single input jumps, flies or flips; timing is synced to music and one mistake restarts the level.

sources.note: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time: automatic jumping
Geometry Dash: rhythm-based action platformer, jump, fly and flip

options.how: Holding the free-run button makes Altair vault and grab handholds automatically; the game picks the next ledge for him.
Hold to charge a jump and release; there is no air control, and a missed landing can drop the knight down large parts of the tower.

sources.note: Assassin's Creed: scale buildings
Jump King: hold to charge, release to jump, higher jumps mean harder falls

options.how: Drake snaps to marked handholds and ledges, so climbing jumps succeed if aimed in roughly the right direction.
Instead of jumping the player flips gravity; spike-lined rooms demand exact flip timing, with instant respawn on death.

sources.note: Uncharted 2: Among Thieves: climbing and platforming
VVVVVV: reversed gravity instead of jumping

options.how: Master Chief walks, crouches and jumps with no sprint (added only in Halo: Reach) and no traversal gear; fights turn on positioning, not mobility.
Pilots wall-run and double jump by default, and the Grapple tactical pulls them across gaps, so maps play as parkour routes.

sources.note: Halo: Combat Evolved: sprint first appeared in Halo: Reach as an armor ability
Titanfall 2: pilots have high mobility via wall-running and double jumping; Apex's Grappling Hook adapted from Titanfall 2's Grapple tactical

options.how: Max moves on foot only; his signature move is a slow-motion dive, so movement serves gunfights rather than reaching new places.
A grappling hook and endless parachute combine: Rico tethers to vehicles and terrain, then glides across a huge island.

sources.note: Max Payne: bullet time, slow-motion gunplay
Just Cause 2: grapple and parachute combo

options.how: Joel walks, runs, crouches and climbs set ledges; gaps need ladders or planks, keeping exploration grounded and slow.
Web-swinging, wall-running and web zips across Manhattan make traversal itself the main pleasure and a skill to master.

sources.note: The Last of Us: store page
Marvel's Spider-Man: web-swing through neighborhoods, fluid urban traversal

options.how: Mario only walks, runs, jumps, swims and climbs vines; springs, lifts and pipes are fixed level props, not tools he carries.
Pablo's grappling hook latches onto anchor blocks to swing and zip across gaps; stages are built around chaining grapples.

sources.note: Super Mario Bros.: controls are walk, run, jump, swim, crouch and climb beanstalks; jumping boards and lifts are level objects
Grapple Dog: use the grappling hook to clear challenges; jumping, swinging and zipping

options.how: Walking in first person through one house; the only verbs are walk, look and interact, keeping focus on objects and clues.
Claire climbs, flies and glides, and golden feathers extend how long she can climb, so the island opens up vertically.

sources.note: Gone Home: first-person exploration of a house
A Short Hike: hike, climb and soar

options.how: Survivors run, jump and crouch along authored paths, so pacing comes from the AI Director, not traversal choices.
Parkour lets players scale nearly any building, and a grappling hook unlocked later pulls them across rooftops away from zombies.

sources.note: Left 4 Dead 2: store page, AI Director
Dying Light: use parkour to scale every building

options.how: Climbable ledges are lighter-colored and signposted, grapple points are wrapped in rope, and a piton is needed for blank walls.
Scouts grab and climb the mountain's rock faces freely, limited by a stamina bar that injuries shrink; pitons and ropes let them rest.

sources.note: Uncharted 4: A Thief's End: Naughty Dog on the handhold and reach system, signposted ledges and pitons
Peak: climbing uses stamina; regenerates while hanging on a piton; injuries limit stamina
Peak: co-op climbing; place ropes and climbing spikes; setbacks limit stamina for climbing

options.how: Lara climbs only marked ledges and planks (faded white paint) and rough, craggy rock walls with her climbing axe; smooth walls are off-limits.
Ezio can scale almost every building or ledge in the cities, so rooftops form free-running routes the player picks.

sources.note: Tomb Raider (2013): Lara can climb walls with a rough stony surface; climbable ledges marked
Assassin's Creed II: run across rooftops and climb the tallest towers
Assassin's Creed II: Ezio scrambles up walls and finds free-running highways

options.game: Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time
options.how: Wall-runs, column climbs and ledge grabs happen only at authored spots, so each room is a traversal puzzle with an intended route.
Spider-Man sticks to and runs along any building surface, so every wall is a path and no route is gated by climbing.

sources.note: Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time: gravity-defying acrobatics
Marvel's Spider-Man: fluid urban traversal

options.how: Jin climbs only designed ledges and holds, and his grappling hook fires only at marked anchor points, so vertical routes are set by designers.
Sable can climb almost any vertical surface on a fast-regenerating stamina meter, and her hover orb removes fall damage.

sources.note: Ghost of Tsushima: the grappling hook only works at specifically marked spots
Sable: climb almost any vertical surface with a stamina meter; no fall damage thanks to the hover orb

options.how: The climber moves ledge to ledge up a largely linear tower route, managing a stamina meter while the rope keeps her secured from fatal falls.
Scouts can grab and scale the mountain's walls anywhere, limited by stamina that injuries shrink; pitons and ropes let teammates rest.

sources.note: Jusant: master climbing tools and watch the stamina meter; ledge-to-ledge climbing, automatically secured; linear progression
Peak: climbing consumes stamina; regenerates while hanging on a piton; letting go and regrabbing the wall
Peak: co-op climbing; place ropes and climbing spikes; setbacks limit stamina for climbing

options.how: Wander grips colossi only at fur patches and ledges, and a grip meter limits holding, so each giant is a set climbing puzzle.
Cole can scale nearly any building in Empire City by grabbing pipes, ledges and signs, so rooftops are always reachable.

sources.note: Shadow of the Colossus: grip and climbing colossi
inFamous: official page

options.how: Cars model weight transfer and tire grip, and players tune suspension, gearing and downforce for each track.
Drifts charge mini-turbo boosts, Smart Steering keeps beginners on track, and items depend on race position.

sources.note: Gran Turismo 7: official site
Mario Kart 8 Deluxe: mini-turbos, Smart Steering, items by distance and placement

note: seed item: accuracy checked by the project owner

options.how: A physics engine with accurate car models on laser-scanned tracks makes braking points, weight transfer and grip the core skill.
Cars drift on demand through loops, wall rides and jumps across asphalt, dirt, ice and plastic; mastering the arcade physics is the puzzle.

sources.note: Assetto Corsa: groundbreaking physics engine, highly accurate car models, laser-scanned tracks
Trackmania: control speed and drift precisely through jumps, loops, wallrides on asphalt, dirt, grass, wood, plastic and ice

options.how: Cars are replicated from laser scans and team data and tracks are laser-scanned to the millimeter, so lifelike physics punish every input.
Charge jumps, rail grinding and wall riding all build mini-turbo boosts, so handling is about chaining tricks for speed, not managing grip.

sources.note: iRacing: lifelike physics; cars replicated from laser scans and team data; tracks laser-scanned with millimeter precision
Mario Kart World: Charge Jump boosts, rail riding charges Mini-Turbos, wall riding

options.how: An uncompromising handling model on surfaces that change under the wheels; crashes cost stage time and repairs are rationed.
Nitro boosts and drifting dominate, and TouchDrive steers automatically so players choose routes and when to boost.

sources.note: DiRT Rally: uncompromising handling model, crashes harm stage time, repairs
Asphalt 9: Legends (now Asphalt Legends): nitro boost, drifting, TouchDrive

options.how: Damage is mostly visual by default and a rewind button undoes crashes, keeping festival driving fast and forgiving.
A soft-body physics engine simulates every vehicle component in real time, so crashes bend frames and break parts.

sources.note: Forza Horizon 5: store page
BeamNG.drive: soft-body physics engine simulating every component in real time

note: seed item: accuracy checked by the project owner

options.how: Damage defaults to cosmetic, so crashes dent the looks but never the performance; mechanical damage is an opt-in Simulation setting.
Metal bends in true-to-life physics as cars collide, and armor plating that protects the body adds weight that changes handling.

sources.note: Forza Horizon 5: damage settings, cosmetic versus simulation damage that affects the car mechanically
Wreckfest: true-to-life physics, new ways for metal to bend; armor protects from damage but adds weight that impacts handling

options.how: Cars never deform or degrade; a demolished car simply respawns on its own side after a few seconds, so contact is a tactic, not a risk.
A free, open-source simulator where vehicles are soft-body structures that flex, bend and deform on impact.

sources.note: Rocket League: demolished state and respawn camera transition
Rocket League: demolished cars respawn on their own side moments later
Rigs of Rods: soft-body physics simulate motion, destruction and deformation of vehicles

options.how: Cars never dent or degrade; a demolition just removes the car for a few seconds before it respawns on its own side of the pitch.
Each car has dozens of deformable parts that bend and tear off, and drivers can be catapulted through the windscreen in big crashes.

sources.note: Rocket League: demolished cars respawn on their own side moments later
FlatOut 2: 40 deformable pieces on every car; driver catapulted through the windscreen

options.how: Kirby can hover for up to 5 seconds to rescue a bad jump, and a defeat only costs Star Coins and restarts the current segment.
Hold to charge and release to leap with no air control; one misjudged jump can drop the knight down screens of hard-won progress.

sources.note: Kirby and the Forgotten Land: hover up to 5 seconds; defeat loses 100 Star Coins and restarts the segment
Jump King: hold to charge and release to leap; once in the air there is no turning back; a mistake means a long fall
